phases.d: Confirm the appointments, gather the proposal and budget, and set up the project filing before you touch the systems.
PMIS step 1, departmental initiation (step 3), D365 set-up, budget approval and activating the project.
Review the contract and proposal within two weeks of work starting and record it on PMIS.
Set the project quality system, record departures through work instructions, and publish the organisation chart.

phases.t: Planning: kick-off, schedule, numbering, codes, risks, lessons
phases.d: The baseline documents the project is controlled against.
Roles, CDE, training and the BEP signing chain, before production starts.
Classification, waivers, champions and targets for PRC-PM-13 and PRC-PM-19.
Weekly progress, design reviews, coordination and correspondence while the design is under way.
The checks EN-01 requires before anything goes to design and safety review or to the client.
Every change request goes through the change log; scope changes go to the PD and may become a claim.
Selecting, controlling and paying suppliers under PRC-PM-10.
For projects where Dar reviews designs prepared by others (PRC-PM-11). PM-02 or PM-04 still applies in full.
What must be true before a package leaves the office, how it is signed and issued, and the reports at the end of each phase.
Closing the design phase in the systems, with the client and in the archive.
PRC-PM-02 Appendix 1. The procedure says these lists may be used as an aide-mémoire, so treat them as checks rather than mandatory steps.

questions.label: Project number
Project title
Project manager
Project director
How will quality be planned for this project?
questions.help: Every project needs quality planning. With QM approval, the full quality plan may be replaced by the Minor Projects procedure (studies and small-scale projects; PM-04 gives no size threshold, so agree it with the QM) or by a work instruction where quality requirements are limited to budgeting and progress monitoring.

questions.label: Will you need to depart from any standard company procedure?
questions.help: Allowed only for client-specific requirements or where the standard is excessive for the project size. Includes a numbering system that differs from PRC-PM-08. It must be agreed in writing with the QM and documented by a project WI or a project-specific procedure.

questions.label: Has the client specified their own quality requirements?
questions.help: If so, the PM passes them to the QM for contract review.

questions.label: What kind of project is it?
questions.help: Drives the BIM procedure (PM-15 for buildings and campus, PM-18 for transportation, both when a transportation project has stations or terminals), the internal gateway (F14) and who leads each component's design.
opts: Transportation with building components (stations, terminals, substations)

questions.label: Is Dar reviewing designs prepared by others (a design review project)?
questions.help: For example reviewing a contractor's or the client's design submittals. PRC-PM-11 then adds its own workflow on top of PM-02 / PM-04.

questions.label: Is there site supervision with a Dar resident engineer (RE)?
questions.help: With an RE, communication and uploads run through the RE (PM-11 §3.1); without, through the area office or client (§3.2).
opts: No, through the area office / client

questions.label: Does the scope include a sewage pump station, fuel farm/station, power plant, electrical substation or data centre?
questions.help: The mechanical GL (pump station, fuel) or the electrical GL (power, substations, data centre) then leads that component's design and checking.

questions.label: Does it include industrial buildings?
questions.help: Adds item 10 of the internal gateway checklist.

questions.label: Does the building scope include car parking?
questions.help: Brings in the transportation design requirements for buildings with parking.

questions.label: Is heavy pedestrian movement expected (large rail or airport terminal, stadium, religious facility, mall)?
questions.help: Pedestrian modelling is then needed at concept stage.

questions.label: Are there basements, deep excavations or other below-ground works where groundwater matters?
questions.help: Brings in the design water table level (DWL) guidelines and the groundwater checks.

questions.label: Is moisture control critical for this project (e.g. GCC climate)?
questions.help: The AR and ME GLs then sign the moisture control checklist PRC-EN-01 (CKL-02) at preliminary and final design.

questions.label: Does Dar's scope include tender documents or BOQs?
questions.help: Brings in PMC's compilation time, BOQ issue control and the tender checklists.

questions.label: Is this a main project with connected sub-projects (e.g. 0100D with 0101D, 0102D)?
Is it a mega project?
questions.help: A PMC planner is allocated to mega projects.

questions.label: Which design process will be used?
questions.help: BIM is mandatory for all building, campus and transportation projects. Not using it needs a derogation approved by the PD, raised by the PM on project-specific grounds.

questions.label: Has the client given exchange information requirements (EIR)?
questions.help: Without a client EIR, Dar BIM standards apply.

questions.label: Is it a large or complex BIM project, or does the client's EIR call for a production or information manager?
What is the project's sustainability level under PRC-PM-13?
questions.help: PRC-PM-13 has no "no sustainability" level: every project is classified at initiation as §4.1, §4.2 or §4.3. §4.1 applies to every project where Dar develops the planning and concept design, even if the contract says nothing about sustainability. If sustainability isn't in the scope of work, you may ask the Sustainability Director to waive the requirements; until the waiver is accepted, §4.1 still applies.
opts: Not in scope of work: ask the SD for a waiver

questions.label: Do the project's categories on PMIS trigger Digital Ready Design?
questions.help: Decided at initiation from the categories and metrics selected on PMIS. If DRD is triggered but you think it shouldn't apply, the PD approves or rejects a waiver.

questions.label: Does the project need a digital solutions scope (DSS)?
Is there a formal signed contract yet?
questions.help: Without one, the information available (even a verbal instruction) must still be reviewed and recorded.

questions.label: Will suppliers or sub-consultants be used?
Are the interfaces complex (more than one external party)?
questions.help: An interface overview chart is then required.

questions.label: Will the project have two PMs?
Will any department have more than one GL from the same unit?
Is the project confidential (by its nature or by client requirement)?
Does the client want hard-copy submissions?
Which office will archive the project?
questions.help: Archiving runs differently in Dar Cairo.

questions.label: Is the design shared between more than one design office?
Will Dar supervise construction after design?
questions.help: Changes what happens to construction follow-up documents at archiving.

questions.label: Include the stage-by-stage aide-mémoire checks?
questions.help: About 37 extra checks from PM-02 Appendix 1, from data collection to final design. Written mainly with building projects in mind.

items.t: Confirm the project number memo naming the PD, PM and APC
items.d: After award the RO, with the AD, creates the project number and title and circulates them by memo to the RD, SL, PD, PM, M&C and APC.

items.t: Get the final technical proposal and commercial budget from the APC
items.d: The APC provides the final submitted or negotiated technical proposal and commercial budget, with the AD's consent. SL and PD are informed.

items.t: Identify statutory and authority requirements
items.d: The APC does this with the PM and the discipline GLs. Confirm the local codes with the GLs at the same time.

items.t: Set up the project filing: PCW, P: drive and hard-copy file
items.d: Open the P: drive folder and sub-folders and have IT create the PCW and its design deliverables QM module. The PCW is the basis of filing; give the PMIS team Edit rights per the permission matrix. Ask for any PCW customisation the project needs.

items.t: Set up the document register and the drawing register
items.d: At start-up, to control every deliverable. The department assistant keeps the document register; allocated staff keep the drawing register. Keep both current.

items.t: Set up hard-copy master files with the department assistants
items.d: PM and each GL keep master files; make the Appendix B filing list project-specific. Stamp client and external correspondence "Copy To Be Preserved".

items.t: Safeguard the data and documents the client provides
items.d: Keep them on the PCW under Project References and Procedures / Other. Report any loss, damage or unsuitability to the client and keep the records.

items.t: Review the proposal-stage information and the contract
items.d: Do this before filling in project initiation on PMIS and D365.

items.t: PMIS step 1: fill in general information
items.d: Project description and components/scope, design office(s), client, director, location, estimated construction cost, date contract signed, work type, man-months contracted, and an image illustrating the project.

items.t: PMIS step 1: fill in classification and metrics
items.d: Category, subcategory and metrics. These also decide whether Digital Ready Design is triggered.

items.t: PMIS step 1: fill in background information
items.d: Groundwater table checking and seismic design requirements (as applicable), items needing special attention, lessons learned from previous projects, source of technical documents, and construction contract information coordinated with PMC.

items.t: Fill the seismic design requirements from the S&B GL's feedback
items.d: The S&B GL coordinates any site-specific requirements with the GHCE GL. Give this special attention at start-up.

items.t: PMIS step 1: record the design process
items.d: Software to be adopted (CADD / BIM / other), selection of the BIM team, and whether DRD applies.

items.t: Get the PD's approval for a BIM derogation
items.d: BIM is mandatory for building, campus and transportation projects. Raise the derogation with the PD on project-specific grounds and keep the approval.

items.t: Have the PD enter contract and payment terms on PMIS
items.d: Contract value, contract type (phase/deliverable, deployment), deliverable fees and payment terms per deliverable are entered by the PD. The billing schedule drives the invoices.

items.t: PMIS step 1: enter the sustainability classification
items.d: §4.1: "Sustainability Driven Planning and Design". §4.2: "Sustainability Goal defined by Client". PM-13 gives no label for §4.3 certification, so confirm the wording on PMIS.

items.t: PMIS step 1: enter firms and suppliers
items.d: Name, scope, involved phases, expected deliverables, status and expected dates, plus the supplier contract.

items.t: List shared suppliers under the main project and map them to sub-projects
items.d: The main PM lists suppliers working across several sub-projects under one contract and identifies their sub-projects. Supplier fees go into each sub-project's WBS and budget as Expenses. Sub-project PMs track the supplier deliverables.

items.t: PMIS step 1: enter other parties (firm and role)
Set the project as confidential
items.d: PCW rights are then limited to the PMIS team.

items.t: D365: fill in general and scheduling information
items.d: Lead department, projected and actual start dates, projected end date, total planned effort in hours, scheduling calendar.

items.t: D365: build the WBS with a budget for every task
items.d: Activities with start and end dates, budget (man-hours and expenses), responsible department(s) and status. Base the budget on the contract or the successful proposal, whichever is available. Supplier fees go in as expenses (ODC).

tip.text: Plan in levels: a Level 1 summary for the whole job, Level 2–3 detail only for the stage you can see. Keeping man-hours per task also gives you the baseline for earned value later.

items.t: D365: distribute budgeted man-hours by department, office and grade
Select the GL Main for each department and notify them to complete PMIS step 3
items.d: GLs Main set up their teams on D365 and re-distribute man-hours by office and grade if needed. Other GLs in the same department get read access.

items.t: Make sure every department's step 3 is complete
items.d: General information (description, design criteria and concept, items needing special attention, lessons learned), the documents and drawings list (expected drawing count at final, tentative list, minimum and proposed IDC requirements), and contract review. Base budget per phase, grade and office plus the team on D365.

items.t: Make sure the GLs Main select the BIM coordinators
items.d: For all trades. The role can be full-time or covered by the GL or the PE/PA.

items.t: Make sure the GLs Main select DRD champions
items.d: With the DRD Lead, once DRD is notified as applicable.

items.t: Define on D365 the roles of each GL from the same unit
Review and approve the departmental initiation (PMIS step 3)
items.d: Once all departments have completed step 3. Settle the clarification register at the same time.

items.t: Import the WBS estimates and submit the total budget for PD approval
items.d: Include the ODC budget. Once the PD approves on D365, set the project to Active. The system sends the initiation report to the SL, AD and APC and makes the budget available to the RO. Only the team assigned on D365 can then charge hours.

items.t: Give the GIS team the project site location through PMIS
items.d: For the GW@DAR database. If it isn't known yet, the system sends monthly reminders; it must be provided before project completion.

items.t: Distribute the contract information to the reviewers
items.d: The PD passes the contract information to the PM; GLs are allocated review responsibilities where the scope is outside the PM's expertise.

items.t: Review the contract and proposal and fill in the contract review on PMIS
items.d: Within two weeks of work starting. Confirm all Dar obligations are met. Each reviewer covers their specialist input and says so if the information is incomplete.

tip.text: Terms worth pulling out for the team: basis of fees, advance payment, reimbursables, monthly vs progress payments, settlement period, retention, set-off, client review periods, suspension and force majeure, termination, professional liability limit, indemnities, and liability for the cost estimate.

items.t: Review whatever information exists, even a verbal instruction, and record it
items.d: Where there is no formal contract, still complete the PMIS contract review with comments based on what is available. Seek clarification and supporting information as needed.

items.t: Log open points in the clarification register and resolve them with the PD or client
items.d: Monitor the register of outstanding items until every one is closed.

items.t: Tell the team that no work proceeds on items awaiting clarification without your written authorisation
items.d: Advise the team of interim actions and notify them of the actions arising from each clarification point.

items.t: Pass the client's quality requirements to the QM for contract review
File the contract review documents
Review the scope of work with the QM to find all applicable quality requirements
Prepare the project quality plan on the PRC-PM-05 (F1) template
items.d: 16 sections: introduction, organisation, definitions, quality policy and objectives, brief, design packaging, phasing and methodology, authorities and requirements, codes and availability, KPIs, documentation numbering, risk, lessons learned, audits, internal QC stages (SDC, IDC, DSR), activities table. Reference the procedures that govern every technical activity. Number it PRJNUM-PLN-PM-DD REV Z.

items.t: Attach the four quality plan appendices
items.d: Risk register, lessons learned register, organisation chart and baseline schedule. Each is valid only at the date of distribution; the latest lives on PCW/PMIS.

items.t: Get the quality policy signed by the PD and the plan authorised by the QM
items.d: The PM signs the plan; the QM authorises it for implementation.

items.t: Agree with the QM, at start-up, to use the Minor Projects procedure
items.d: PM-04 replaces the full quality system only by agreement with the company QM.

items.t: Make PRC-PM-04 project-specific and fill in its Appendix A
items.d: Add the project number; list the applicable company procedures on the cover page if there are deliverables. Appendix A: scope, authorities and their requirements, codes and availability, DSR required or not, documents in other languages, OC, schedule, risk register, lessons register. PM and QM sign the authorisation record; the PD signs the quality policy.

items.t: Set up the checking system for a minor project
items.d: Every deliverable is checked by a competent engineer who isn't the originator; the check copy is marked and initialled. Keep IDC comments until project completion.

items.t: Prepare a work instruction to replace the quality plan and get QM approval
items.d: Lists the applicable procedures and requirements where quality requirements are limited to budgeting and progress monitoring. Number it PRJNUM-WI-XX.

items.t: Post the approved quality document on the PCW, register it and notify the team
items.d: Post under Project References & Procedures > Manuals and procedures. Distribute to the PD, QM, APC and project GLs. Register it as a PM document in the lead department's document registry.

items.t: Agree each departure from a standard procedure in writing with the QM
items.d: Only for client-specific requirements or where the standard is excessive for the project size. Quality must not be compromised.

items.t: Issue a project work instruction for each approved departure
items.d: Number it PRJNUM-WI-XX (e.g. S19070-0100D-WI-01). It must cross-reference the parent procedure and be reviewed and approved by the QM. Post it on the PCW and issue it to the team, copying the QM.

items.t: Or make the company procedure project-specific
items.d: Revise it and add the project number in the footer (e.g. S19070-0100D-PRC-EN-02). The QM processes and approves it.

items.t: Request extra QMS training for the team if needed
items.d: Quality management runs training under PRC-QA-03.

items.t: Prepare the project organisation chart (OC)
items.d: Positions and personnel assigned to the project, up to and including the client and any suppliers, all GLs and the APC. Show the revision and date.

tip.text: Use the chart to settle the PM / functional manager split early: the PM controls project time and cost, each GL controls time, cost and quality of their own sub-tasks, and trade-offs are agreed jointly.

items.t: Publish the OC on PMIS
items.d: The team is notified automatically. If the chart isn't generated from PMIS, sign it, include revision and date, post it on the PCW and notify the team.

items.t: Show each PM's responsibilities on the OC
Include a specification coordinator in the AR team
items.d: Per the Specifications procedure PRC-EN-03.

items.t: Show the sustainability leader and the sustainability champions on the OC
items.d: PM-02 names the sustainability leader; PM-13 adds the champions of each trade.

items.t: Show the BIM team on the OC
items.d: BIM Manager, BIM coordinators and any production / information manager.

items.t: Add the suppliers to the OC
Make sure every team member knows their project obligations
Prepare an interface overview chart and circulate it to the team
items.d: Shows the interfaces with all external parties, including points of contact.

items.t: Confirm who leads each component's design
items.d: The AR GL leads the building components and the infrastructure GL leads the infrastructure components: code compliance, SDC, IDC and level of detail before submission to the PM. Overall management stays with the lead department.

items.t: Confirm the ME or EL GL leads the special facility component
items.d: Mechanical GL for sewage pump stations and fuel farms/stations; electrical GL for power plants, substations and data centres. They make sure SDC, IDC and BIM requirements are met before submitting to the PM.

items.t: Hold the kick-off meeting to review the scope with the team
items.d: Prepare the minutes, sign and post them on the PCW, and issue them to the trades.

tip.text: Use the kick-off to fix the communication channels: who issues instructions, how reviews and approvals flow between disciplines, and how sub-consultants are coordinated.

items.t: Raise the groundwater table at kick-off
items.d: Make sure all involved departments use the design water table level guidelines in Appendix 2 (GHCE, WE, S&B and AR interfaces).

items.t: Prepare the baseline schedule with the PD
items.d: Show all key activities and milestones, including the Preliminary and Final DSR and the DDRs where applicable.

tip.text: Rolling-wave planning: detail only a few weeks ahead and refine as the brief firms up. Build in client review periods and authority approval time so the dates are realistic.

items.t: Add a final model-based coordination one week before each submission
Agree with PMC the time they need to compile the tender documents
items.d: Including non-technical reviews (formatting, headers, footers, presentation) before submission. Agree it per project based on scope and number of deliverables, and show it in the schedule.

items.t: Put the certification online-submission dates in the schedule
items.d: The sustainability leader coordinates the dates with you.

items.t: Sign the baseline schedule and post it on the PCW
items.d: Show the revision code and date. Notify the AD, PD, GLs, APC and QM.

items.t: Get a PMC planner allocated
items.d: The planner updates the schedule, flags foreseen delays and proposes mitigation.

items.t: If no schedule can be built, tell the team the expected completion date and the contractual limit for actioning submittals
Set the documentation numbering system and instruct the team
items.d: Documents: PRJNUM-PH-BBB-CC-DD REV Z (PH = CD/PD/DD/FD/TD; BBB = document type such as SPC, BOQ, RPT, MOM; CC = department). Drawings: PRJNUM-PH-C-XNN, or PRJNUM-PH-C-NNN without a sheet type. Client contractual numbering takes precedence. Record it in the quality plan §11.

items.t: Issue a QM-approved work instruction for any numbering that differs from PRC-PM-08
items.d: Also give the team your instructions on revision type (alphabetical or numeric), the Description attribute and a header/footer sample. PM-08 has no "WI" document type, so agree the WI's own number with the QM.

items.t: Authorise the design codes and standards
items.d: GLs pick the international and country codes for their departments using the PCW tool. Approve the applicable ones and reject unauthorised or superseded codes, giving the reason. Engineers may use only the codes you authorised.

tip.text: Include the authority and permit codes, not just design codes: the consultant is expected to design to the requirements of every authority having jurisdiction.

items.t: Send codes missing from the country codes database to the library unit
Have the GLs enter their department risks in the PCW risk tool
items.d: At start-up. Categories: technical, organisational, project management, HSSE, information security, other.

items.t: Review and approve the GLs' risks and add the project management risks
items.d: Each risk: cause, consequence, probability and impact (1–5), rating, owner, mitigation and residual rating.

items.t: Publish the risk register and distribute it
items.d: Generate it under the "published register" tab. Send to the PD, AD, APC and GLs and attach it to the quality plan or PM-04.

items.t: Get the PD or the client to accept any residual risk that stays high
Search the PMIS lessons-learned database with the GLs
items.d: List the valid lessons under "lessons learned from previous projects" on PMIS and share the relevant ones with the team.

tip.text: Knowledge leaves with people. Pull the lessons into actions the team will actually see (risk register lines, checklist items) rather than leaving them in a list.

items.t: Set up the lessons learned register
items.d: Revision control is alphabetical (A, B, C) for internal issues and numerical (0, 1, 2) for external issues.

items.t: Give the ME GL the schedule, road map and latest country code
items.d: Where there are no local codes, agree the codes and employer guidelines with the ME GL, the area office and fire & life safety.

items.t: Assign the project BIM Manager
items.d: From the lead trade, with at least one BIM project of experience.

items.t: Agree whether the Lead BIM Manager comes from the Digital Practice Unit
items.d: An option for large, complex or advanced-BIM building projects.

items.t: Assign a production manager (and an information manager on building projects)
items.d: For big-scale projects, or where the client's EIR asks for them.

items.t: Assign an Architecture BIM Manager for the building components
items.d: PM-15 governs the building components. The TR Lead BIM Manager and the AR BIM Manager manage the interface together and sign a joint BEP.

items.t: Ask the DPU to assign the Lead BIM Specialist and the BIM specialists team
Hold the BIM kick-off meeting
items.d: Introduce the scope, milestones and EIR to the team (and the BIM specialists on building projects). Issue minutes.

items.t: Tell the team Dar BIM standards apply in the absence of a client EIR
Define the project composition type
items.d: Building: single building, multi-building or campus. Transportation: highway, road, airport/heliport, rail or port.

items.t: Ask IT to set up the project CDE and install the BIM tools
items.d: Shared drive and PCW folder structure per project category; tools such as BIMcollab.

items.t: Arrange BIM training or awareness sessions if needed
items.d: Revit, Civil3D, Navisworks, BIMcollab, the BEP, iLOD, roles and folder structure, per the Dar training plan.

items.t: Give the BIM Manager your input on BIM requirements and standards
items.d: Model breakdown strategy, naming and presentation standards, title block.

items.t: Develop the BIM Execution Plan with the BIM Manager
items.d: On the PRC-PM-15 (F1) template (also used for transportation). Includes the RACI, a supplier EIR if there are suppliers, and the TIDPs combined into the MIDP. It is read together with the quality plan.

items.t: Check and sign the BEP, then get the PD's approval
items.d: BIM Manager signs "By" → you request changes until it's final and sign "Checked by" (on building projects with the Lead BIM Specialist) → PD signs "Approved by".

items.t: Post the BEP on the PCW, issue it and register it
items.d: Issue to the team copying the PD and QM; register it in the document registry. You must be copied whenever the BIM Manager issues a revision. Keep it current: it is a living document.

items.t: Confirm with the QM which BIM procedure applies
items.d: PM-15 covers building and campus projects and PM-18 transportation; neither names other infrastructure.

items.t: Give suppliers PCW access and the supplier EIR
items.d: Suppliers upload to their PCW directory; external files are quarantined (Shared_Ext) until the assigned trade checks them.

items.t: Review the scope of work and confirm the sustainability level with the client
items.d: §4.1 driven by Dar's planning and concept, §4.2 goals set by the client, or §4.3 certification.

items.t: Ask the Sustainability Director to waive the sustainability requirements
items.d: PM-13 has no "not applicable" option, so the requirements stay unless they're waived. Give a valid justification (e.g. not in the scope of work); the notification goes to the SD for review. If the SD doesn't accept it, change the sustainability answer to §4.1: it applies wherever Dar develops the planning and concept design.

items.t: Make sure the Sustainability Director appoints the sustainability leader (SLD)
items.d: At project initiation.

items.t: Brief the SLD and tell the team the sustainability goals
items.d: Exact location, expected area programme, client requirements and anything else that affects sustainability.

items.t: Agree the goals and KPIs the SLD proposes
items.d: The SLD then assigns the sustainability coordinator (SCO).

items.t: Make sure every trade has a sustainability champion (SC)
items.d: The SCO coordinates with the GLs to assign them; each SC needs experience of at least one relevant sustainable project.

items.t: Hold the integrated design charrette with all parties
items.d: After project initiation, led by the SLD with you.

items.t: Make sure the KPI list is registered on the PCW
Make sure the coordinated certification checklist is prepared and agreed
items.d: The SLD gives the SCO a tentative checklist; the SCO coordinates it with the champions and assigns responsibilities. Number it per PRC-PM-08 with CKL and SUS.

items.t: Make sure the certification cost has been assessed
items.d: By the relevant department or a cost consultant, in line with the contract.

items.t: Agree the TR / sustainability lead and support split
items.d: Per the App. 2.6 matrix: stakeholder engagement, alignment, earthworks balance, multimodal, climate resilience, noise, micro-simulation, KPIs. Infrastructure certifications (Envision, BREEAM, SITES) are led by the sustainability team.

items.t: Record on PMIS whether DRD applies
items.d: Based on the categories and metrics identified at initiation. Once listed as applicable, make sure the DRD Lead and DRD Interface Manager are notified.

items.t: Request the DRD waiver with a valid justification
items.d: The PD approves or rejects it on PMIS.

items.t: Engage Digital Solutions & Services (DSS) for the digital scope
Make sure each GL Main reports progress on D365 every week
items.d: Progress %, abortive work, problems and proposed solutions, foreseen delays, comments and team. Then approve the departmental progress and complete the PM progress report.

tip.text: Read CPI and SPI together: earned value compares the budget of work actually done against both the plan and the hours spent, so you see a slip before it shows in the dates.

items.t: Reconfirm the status and dates of every deliverable in the WBS
items.d: Not Started, In Process, On Hold, Submitted, Approved as noted, Approved. Progress can't be reported on Not Started or On Hold; Approved counts as 100%.

items.t: Review the PMIS dashboard: CPI, SPI and EAC
Update the progress of involved suppliers
items.d: Under project initiation / firms and suppliers.

items.t: Make sure GLs approve team timecards weekly
items.d: Block timecards by phase, task, office or department where needed.

items.t: Hold the design development reviews (DDRs) and issue minutes
items.d: Call all or part of the team as scheduled; the minutes are the record.

items.t: Hold model-based DDRs every week
items.d: Cover the coordination requirements of PRC-PM-15. Issue minutes.

items.t: Hold model-based DDRs every two weeks
items.d: Cover the coordination requirements of PRC-PM-18 (and PM-15 for the building components). Issue minutes.

items.t: Freeze design changes one week before each submission
items.d: From schematic design onwards. Put the whole team's effort into final model-based coordination and clash resolution.

items.t: Make sure the federated model and clash detection run at the BEP frequency
items.d: Federated model maintained as trade models are published; clash detection per the clash matrix; issues raised in BIMcollab and resolved iteratively.
items.who: BIM Manager / coordinators; PM / GLs resolve

items.t: Make sure model QA and BIM SDC are done and the SDC covers signed
items.d: Model check reports count as the SDC reports. The GL and BIM coordinator sign the SDC cover and post it on the PCW.

items.t: Follow up the monthly BIM compliance review
items.d: The reviewer signs the compliance report and sends it to the BIM Manager for corrective action; it's posted on the PCW.

items.t: Add BIM risks and lessons to the project registers
items.d: The BIM Manager and coordinators report them to you and the GLs.

items.t: Make sure AR and TR apply the transportation requirements for buildings with parking
items.d: Entrance and exit geometry, vehicle types, ramps, stalls, aisles, clearances, gradients, signage, entries and booths, pedestrian capacity and traffic simulation. TR attends coordination meetings and continues IDC through preliminary and final design.

items.t: Have TR arrange a traffic impact study (TIS) at concept stage
items.d: Appendix 3 requires a TIS for all new buildings regardless of size, following local requirements.

items.t: Have TR prepare pedestrian modelling during concept design
Make sure TR prepares the composite drawings
items.d: Combining all related departments (street lighting, crossings and ramps, trees, signs, utilities). They're subject to IDC and DSR and signed by reviewers and designers.

items.t: Hold the sustainability meeting at planning / concept stage
items.d: The SCO attends with all parties and makes sure the GLs deliver. Calls or emails can replace it.

items.t: Hold a sustainability meeting at each design phase
items.d: Checks progress against targets. You may agree to skip it for a stage with no changes affecting sustainability; calls or emails can replace it.

items.t: Make sure the mandatory sustainability analyses are done
items.d: AR: climate and microclimate, energy, daylight, thermal comfort, onsite renewables. PUD/landscape: also outdoor thermal comfort, water demand and supply, stormwater. Depth varies by stage.

items.t: Make sure the KPI tracker is completed each design phase
items.d: Champions submit it to the SCO and report changes.

items.t: Follow the online certification submissions
items.d: The SCO follows up the team and champions; the SLD briefs you on status.

items.t: Make sure the DRD checklist is filled on the PCW before the first submission
items.d: Filled by the departmental GLs and validated by the DRD champions; keep it updated throughout.

items.t: Investigate every schedule delay and agree mitigation with the PD
items.d: Inform the SL, AD and APC.

items.t: Revise the baseline schedule only when allowed, and redistribute it
items.d: Only for a change to the contracted scope, or when actual progress has drifted so far that the baseline is no longer meaningful. Upload each new revision to the PCW, copying the AD, PD, APC and QM.

items.t: Keep the control documents current
items.d: Update when needed: organisation chart, work instructions, project schedule, quality plan (numbering section included), risk register, lessons learned register.

items.t: Keep the design codes list reviewed and updated
Review and re-publish the risk register at each phase end or new risk
items.d: Redistribute it to the PD, AD, APC and GLs. Tick "show in client report" for any risks you share with the client.

items.t: Identify lessons learned with the GLs at the end of each phase
items.d: Log them in the register and track their action plans. Schedule a lessons learned workshop if one is needed. Liaise with the area manager/coordinator to collect lessons throughout.

items.t: Sign the correspondence to the client and area manager
items.d: Every outgoing item carries the project number and a reference. Contractual and schedule communications are copied to you.

items.t: Issue minutes and transmittals on the project forms
items.d: Minutes go to all attendees promptly and become final if there are no comments. Transmittals are used for information, approval, comment or IDC.

items.t: Make sure the team files email through EFS and submits deliverables through the PCW
Close any QM audit findings (CARs) within the allocated time
items.d: The QM audits the project to its audit schedule; rectify each CAR and prevent recurrence.

items.t: Copy the QM on quality problems
items.d: For example lack of response from other departments or inadequate checking.

items.t: Bring anything that may be a customer complaint to the AD/AM
Set the project status on D365 when work pauses
items.d: Pending for short or review periods; On Hold when long inactivity is expected.

items.t: Make sure each GL completes single departmental checking
items.d: The originating department's GL checks work definition, methods, accuracy, document quality and conflicts. Where a department has only one specialist engineer, the DD, HOD or a nominee checks.

items.t: Collect the signed SDC checklists and the deliverables quality checklist
items.d: One single departmental checklist per department (CKL-01, CKL-04 to CKL-14 by trade) and CKL-03 from the PE/A for each submission, submitted with the deliverables and kept on the PCW.

items.t: Get the moisture control checklist signed by the AR and ME GLs
items.d: At preliminary design and at final design; the AR GL submits it to you.

items.t: Make sure every interfacing document gets inter-departmental checking (IDC)
items.d: To the minimum IDC requirements declared at initiation. IDC is held at least once before the final design submission. Specs, BOQs, MoM and manuals use the IDC table of contents and signature cover page; drawings are marked up and re-issued at a new revision.

items.t: Run IDC before the schematic / preliminary submission as well
Make sure IDC comments are closed out and the evidence is on the PCW
items.d: Each comment is marked implemented or discarded; the GL initials discarded ones with the reason. The PCW holds the email to reviewers and their reply. Keep originals until project completion.

items.t: Make sure BIM IDC is done at least once per phase and the IDC covers signed
items.d: Clash detection and BIMcollab reports count as the IDC reports. GLs state why any issue is pending; the BIM Manager agrees an action plan, signs, posts on the PCW and informs you.

items.t: Start BIM QC before each client submission
items.d: Email the BIM QC team and share the BEP and models. Required at least once per design phase before submission, even if the client wants no model.

items.t: Check the BIM QC summary report, close its issues and sign F4
items.d: Inform the GLs and make sure every issue is resolved before final submission. F4 is signed by QC, the BIM Manager and you, posted on the PCW and issued for DSR.

items.t: Request the DSR and define its scope
items.d: Send the full set of drawings and documents with the document list. The PD/PM assigns the review team leader, who assigns reviewers from the related departments. Schedule it with the team leader.

items.t: Make sure everything is checked and IDC'd before the DSR starts
items.d: The checker verifies IDC comments were incorporated. EL/TL and ME single departmental checklists must be with the DSR reviewers before it starts.

items.t: Add the final-DSR extras to the package
items.d: BIM model reports and QC summary for BIM projects; the DRD checklist validated by each champion for DRD projects; signed composite drawings for transportation.

items.t: Hold the preliminary and final design and safety reviews (DSR)
items.d: The review team leader issues the DRARs and DSR report to you. Close the DRARs and send the compiled report to the PD and QM. At preliminary DSR, minutes alone are enough.

tip.text: Synthesise the review the way the client's reviewer will: complete against the contract list, compliant with regulations, consistent with the client's criteria, at the right level of detail for the stage, and coordinated across disciplines.

items.t: Make sure the certification checklist is signed and issued each phase
items.d: Champions complete and sign, the SCO reviews and signs, the SLD signs; the SCO posts it on the PCW copying you and the SLD.

items.t: Make sure trade reports and specs carry their sustainability content
items.d: Each trade report has a Sustainability Aspirations section; specifications carry the SUS requirements; sustainability items are recommended in the SDC checklists.

items.t: Make sure each DRD champion completes the final checklist review at DSR
items.d: Submitted to the DRD Lead and Interface Manager. Validate the DRD status with the Interface Manager.

items.t: Log every design change request in the change log on the PCW
items.d: From any stakeholder. The PD reviews each request.

tip.text: For every change ask three questions before you agree: what exactly does it involve, what does it do to the design schedule and fees, and is there a viable solution? Filter out unnecessary changes with the functional managers.

items.t: Get each GL's man-hour and schedule impact for the change
items.d: When you instruct a change, the GLs review its impact and inform you (PRC-EN-09). Checking of the revised design can be limited to the change and associated documents.

items.t: Raise anything that may change the contract scope with the PD
items.d: Especially where it affects schedule, man-hours or abortive work. Follow PRC-PM-06.

items.t: Process approved changes as design change notes (DCNs) on PMIS
items.d: Update the DCN details, assess the impact with the department director, have GLs fill in and submit their DCNs, and review and approve the DCNs submitted by the trades (PRC-EN-09).

items.t: Prepare the claim when the PD and AD decide one is needed
items.d: The PD assesses changes with the AD. You prepare the claim; the AD/APC reviews it and submits it for client approval. If the AD decides to proceed without a claim, record that.

items.t: After the client approves the claim, create the DCN and update the contract terms
items.d: Create the design change note on PMIS (PRC-EN-09). The PD updates contract and payment terms on PMIS and the AD approves them.

items.t: Make sure revisions follow the revision rules
items.d: No revised issue without a new code; superseded items marked. Alphabetical (A, B, C) before the approved issue, numeric (0, 1, 2) from it. Clouds on drawings, margin lines on text, quote the DCN number. Keep Rev 0 and later revisions for the project duration.

items.t: Check changes against the sustainability targets
items.d: The SLD advises you of changes affecting targets and the checklist is updated. If the client adds sustainability scope after concept, move the project to §4.2 or §4.3.

items.t: Keep all contract variation correspondence in the project files
Identify the need for each supplier and prepare its scope
items.d: The originating engineer writes the full scope into the contract documents and flows requirements down to any sub-sub-contractor. Coordinate selection with the originating engineer.

items.t: Get the technical evaluation (TE) completed
items.d: The originating engineer completes F1 (with IDC if other disciplines' input is needed); the DD reviews it and it goes to the PD, PM and QM.

items.t: Check the supplier against the approved supplier database
items.d: Approved: check ISO 9001 validity, that the scope matches, and previous performance reports (F3). Not approved: send the QA questionnaire (F4); the QE prepares the QA evaluation (F2), the QM reviews it, and the RO creates the supplier ID.

items.t: Apply the same controls to client-nominated suppliers
items.d: If they don't return the QA questionnaire, Dar reviews their deliverables as the controlling procedure.

items.t: Make sure each supplier contract has a full specification of work and names its quality system
items.d: Notify the DD, PD, PM and QM of the selected supplier. If the QM recommends an audit, the QM and PD agree it.

items.t: Ask for a renewed ISO 9001 certificate if it expires during the project
Check each supplier invoice before paying
items.d: Is it in line with progress, payment terms and the client agreement? If so, prepare the billing details for PD approval; the system sends them to the RO and AD.

items.t: Get the supplier performance report completed when their task is finished
items.d: The originating engineer completes F3, the DD reviews it, and it goes to the QM and PM to update the database.

items.t: Agree the communication channels with the RE
items.d: Advise the team and the QM.

items.t: Agree the communication channels with the area office or client
items.d: Advise the team and the QM.

items.t: Hold the design review kick-off with the GLs
items.d: Review the scope and agree the review process. The RE may be invited.

items.t: Make sure every received submittal is uploaded to the PCW
items.d: If the other party won't use the platform, upload for them and return comments by email or FTP.

items.t: Assign each submittal to a lead trade and the involved trades, with a deadline
items.d: The lead trade compiles comments (with IDC as needed) and proposes a status: Approved, Approved as noted, Revise and resubmit, Rejected.

items.t: Review the comments with the GLs and set the final code
items.d: With PMC if applicable; a meeting is optional.

items.t: Send the final reply and repeat until all comments are cleared
items.d: Through the PCW, to the contractor (via the RE) or to the client / area office.

items.t: Review the pending submittals every week
If you don't use the automated review platform, keep the comments matrix by hand
items.d: The PCW is then used for filing only, with manual logs and the comments matrix (action codes I/N/T, acceptance Y/N/O).

items.t: Get internal gateway approval before issuing the preliminary / schematic design
items.d: The AR GL and PM fill the F14 checklist (IDC, DSR minutes, risk register, sustainability, acoustics, fire & life safety, envelope, codes, moisture control) and submit it to the PD and the Architecture Design Principal or Director. Post the approved checklist on the PCW.

items.t: Attach the moisture control checklist to the gateway approval
For industrial buildings, review operations with the Industrial Unit Principal Engineer
items.d: F14 item 10: clearances, door heights, bay depth, dangerous goods storage, waste, mechanical systems, cranes, network connections.

items.t: Make sure documents carry the right signatures for the revision type
items.d: Checked before leaving the department and signed "By". Alphabetical revisions to the client: originator and checker. Rev 0 or any numeric revision: approved by the DD or HOD. The GL signs the revision approval box before any external submission.

items.t: Stamp drawings leaving the company
items.d: For Construction, For Tender or For Information (other stamps on your request). For Information: designed by PE/A and checked by GL. For Tender or Construction: also approved by the DD/HOD. Tender to Construction with no change keeps the revision and changes only the stamp.

items.t: Control the BOQ and tender issue
items.d: Same version to every party, in PDF and protected Excel, with a record of recipients. Tables of contents and IDC forms (PRC-EN-03 (F1A), PRC-EN-05 (F1A), (F3A)) signed at submission. Evaluation criteria and form of conditions approved by the client.

items.t: Give PMC a copy of the tender documents for constructability review
Set up the electronic submittal
items.d: Advise the GLs; collect PDF or DWF copies; keep the signed hard copy in the project file (or the signed PDF on the project website); send a sample to the area office to test production.

items.t: Keep an e-paper copy of every submittal on the W: drive
items.d: Label the storage location as in PM-12 Appendix A. Send native files zipped only if the area office asks.

items.t: Issue hard copies under a cover letter
Authorise the information model and run the BEP submission process
items.d: Compile the submittal on the P: drive per the submission folder structure, prepare the MIDP for the package, run the health check list, upload to the PCW/CDE for area office or client acceptance.

items.t: Do a full risk register review before the final submission
items.d: With the GLs if needed. F11 asks whether all risks are mitigated and closed.

items.t: Fill in the PM checklist for project submittal (F11) and authorise release
items.d: Covers SDC and quality checklists, IDC before Rev 0 with signed tables of contents, design reviews and DRARs, risk register, groundwater, moisture control, contract milestone, client and regulatory requirements. Post on the PCW; send to the PD, PMC and QM.

tip.text: Before release, check it the way the client's reviewer will: complete against the contract list, compliant with regulations, consistent with the client's criteria, at the right level of detail for the stage, and coordinated across disciplines.

items.t: Attach the moisture control checklist to the F11 at final submission
Request a sustainability report where needed
items.d: The SCO prepares it and the SLD reviews it (PRC-EN-11). It can be a section of the design report.

items.t: Complete the phase completion report (PhCR) at the end of each phase
items.d: The system initiates it. Each GL fills a departmental PhCR (design and quality problems, budget deviation, lessons learned, drawing count against the register); you approve them and fill the PM PhCR, adding complaints and the location of the latest submittal and 3D visuals.

items.t: Raise the invoice when a payment falls due
items.d: Create the payment milestone linked to the deliverable's payment terms (PMIS step 1, contract and payment terms tab), then initiate the invoice to the RO. Keep the APC informed of billing status if needed.

items.t: Set the project as Completed on D365
Get every GL Main to fill the departmental project completion report (PCR)
items.d: Design and quality problems, budget deviation, lessons learned (sent to departmental reviewers for validation), final drawing count against the register. Approve each one.

items.t: Have the GLs summarise lessons learned for the departmental checkers
items.d: Your own lessons are filled once all departmental lessons are validated, including those collected with the area manager/coordinator.

items.t: Finalise the PM PCR
items.d: Design and quality problems, complaints, budget deviation, lessons learned. The system then sends the PCR and the lessons learned report, and creates the archive repository.

items.t: Record the sustainability strategy or rating achieved in the PM PCR
items.d: Strategy achieved for §4.1/§4.2; certification rating achieved for §4.3. For certification, make sure the SLD posts the certificate on the PCW and issues it to the AD, PD, PM and M&C.

items.t: Acknowledge in the PM PCR that DRD was incorporated
items.d: GLs may pass new use cases to the DRD unit for the master checklist.

items.t: Send the customer satisfaction questionnaire to the APC
items.d: Copy the AD and PD. The AD validates the feedback and the APC distributes it.

items.t: Prepare the client certificate with M&C and the APC
items.d: The AD approves it before the APC submits it to the client.

items.t: Confirm the GIS team has the project site location
Fill in the archive initiation information on Archives@Dar
items.d: Completing the PCR creates the repository and emails you. Enter project, package, phase, submission date, revision and content type; the GLs then get their tasks.

items.t: Make sure the GLs upload their deliverables and working files, then close the archive
items.d: Valid file names; working files copied to \\db-cfs\P-Archives\[ProjectNo]\[Trade]. Tasks are due in four weeks. Fix anything the archive admin reports; the folder then becomes read-only.

items.t: Run the Dar Cairo archiving steps
items.d: Issue F2; have the draftsmen deposit drawings renamed per the archiving convention; check the trades' Excel lists follow the archiving memo format; issue F1 certifying the files are complete; resolve discrepancies; then tell the draftsmen when to delete from the P: drive.

items.t: Archive in the main design office
items.d: Other offices send their files with an Excel metadata list.

items.t: Archive the hard copies and the latest registers
items.d: With no Dar construction supervision: archive the electronic files plus the latest drawing and document registers; one hard copy stamped "archive" goes to the archive section (a second stays with you if the PD instructs); request transfer of the hard-copy project files for scanning.

items.t: Keep the construction follow-up documents in the design department / PMC
items.d: The GL may send selected files to the archive in coordination with you; full archiving follows after construction.

items.t: Data collection: formal acceptance received for the scope in the proposal
Data collection: site visit team nominated (with the AM)
Data collection: building regulations and local or accepted international codes available for every discipline
Data collection: sustainability scope defined
Data collection: topographic and survey maps available and matching the client's
Data collection: geotechnical data given to the departments; groundwater checked by GHCE and WE; seismic requirements checked
Data collection: climatic data, local construction practice, local materials and plot boundary conditions known
Data collection: specialist consultants identified, with agreements covering technical and quality scope, and their data available
Data collection: AM has no comments on the scope, or their comments and the time/cost impact are settled
Data collection: information collated and sent to all departments, and every department confirms it can start
items.d: Consider a meeting with department representatives on the outcome.

items.t: Pre-design: each department (and consultant) has reported on data collection and accepted the scope
Pre-design: scope fully defined and matching the proposal, or the time/cost impact agreed with the AM
Pre-design: instruction issued to the design departments to start conceptual design
Concept: minuted meetings held with designers on the systems they intend to adopt
Concept: meetings held with local authorities for approval of the concept
Concept: team queries answered promptly through the AM, and replies checked
Concept: list of drawings received from each department, matching the proposal scope
Concept: specialist consultants' input received on time
Concept: deliverables compared with the scope and initiation requirements before sending to the AM
Preliminary: AM approval of the concept received, or out-of-scope requests handled as a variation (PRC-PM-06)
Preliminary: written instruction issued to start design development, including AM comments
Preliminary: revised man-hour schedules received and accepted; project schedule updated and distributed
Preliminary: geotechnical investigation scoped and commissioned
Preliminary: regular minuted coordination meetings with at least one member per department
Preliminary: outline specs drafted in the TOR format and performance-spec items identified
Preliminary: form of client/contractor contract confirmed and schedule milestones confirmed
Preliminary: PMC's view on the constructability of the selected systems obtained
Preliminary: written confirmation that departments follow local regulations
Preliminary: excavation limits, slopes and foundation levels confirmed acceptable geotechnically
Preliminary: design coordinated across departments; EL has ME loads in writing; S&B loads match AR space use and MEP systems
Preliminary: external works on schedule; permit regulations known and complied with; correct number of copies prepared
Final: client approval of the preliminary design received, or out-of-scope requests handled through design change control (PRC-EN-09)
Final: client comments circulated to departments for man-hour/schedule impact; revised figures accepted and agreed with the client
Final: order to proceed with variations issued after client approval; schedule updated and distributed
Final: coordination between designers completed (DSR, PRC-EN-07); electrical loads match mechanical requirements
Final: correct number of tender document copies issued per TOR
Final: building permit issued and local approvals secured
